::: {#def-spearman-r}
#### Spearman rank correlation

Replace each $x_i$ by its rank among $x_1, \ldots, x_n$,
and each $y_i$ by its rank among $y_1, \ldots, y_n$,
giving tied values the average of the ranks they span.
The **Spearman rank correlation** $r_S$ is the
[Pearson correlation coefficient](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-pearson-r)
of the ranks.
:::

::: notes
Because ranks depend only on the ordering of the values,
$r_S$ measures how close the association is to monotone,
whether or not it is linear,
and a single extreme value moves $r_S$ less than it moves $r$.
:::
